rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 and 3 - authors designed, built and field-tested a solar-powered gravity-fed micro-tube irrigation system at the CRIDA research farm, Hyderabad, recording emitter discharges. Q2: Section 3.1-3.4 and Table 5 - own measurements give overall emitter flow variation 18.96%, CUC 93.65% and Du 91.55%, all within ASAE limits, i.e. the exact figures in the passage. Q4: Sections 2.3-2.4, Tables 3-4 and Section 4 - head losses in main, laterals and micro-tubes were computed with Darcy-Weisbach/orifice equations and the authors attribute the low emitter-flow variation to negligible conveyance head loss and the constant-pressure equilibrium tank. Q7: Sections 3.5 and 4 - from own sediment sampling the authors state that only water from the top 3/4 of pond depth should be used and the system run 72 h after runoff events to avoid clogging; laminar flow must be maintained in all pipe sections; design is specific to farm size. Q9: Table 5 and Sections 3.1-3.4 - CV of emitter discharge 5.40%, CD at 5% = 0.16, emitter discharge range 0.801-1.034 L/h, lateral-wise ranges of qvar, CUC (90.9-96.2%) and Du (88.3-94.6%).
rows.notes: The study measures application uniformity (qvar, CUC, Du), which is what the passage reports; it does not measure actual water savings or compare water use against another irrigation method, so 'water conservation' is only inferred from uniformity. Single site, single plot (18 m x 11 m), one method (catch-can style emitter discharge measurement) - no triangulation. Q4 given on the basis that head loss/pressure distribution (the intermediate variable for uniformity) was modelled and used to explain the result, though the model was not itself validated. Q8 'no': the authors note the study was site-specific and that acreage figures are indicative, but frame this as grounds for replication rather than as a limitation of the uniformity result.

notes: Full text appears complete. Study is a design-and-evaluation paper for a low-cost solar-pumped gravity-fed micro-tube (drip-type) system; the only field results are hydraulic uniformity metrics and pond water sediment/quality, with no crop, yield or water-saving data.
